summary: Module 3 BREAK: The Convention Violation -- empirical error-format comparison. Methodology: ran live error-path probes against both an EXISTING endpoint (/links) and the agent's TEAM endpoints (/teams, /teams/{id}/members) and compared the JSON error envelopes byte-for-byte. FINDINGS: all six team error paths produce the SAME shape as existing endpoints: 400 {error:{code:request_invalid,message:'invalid request',request_id}} (validation: empty name, missing name, bad role, invalid email), 401 {error:{code:unauthorized,...}}, 403 {error:{code:forbidden,message:'team admin required'/'team owner required'}}, 404 {error:{code:not_found,message:'team not found'/'user not found'}}, 409 {error:{code:conflict,message:'user is already a member'}}. This is BY CONSTRUCTION consistent: every team endpoint raises HTTPException (or triggers RequestValidationError) which main.py's exception handlers wrap in error_envelope -- identical to links.py. WHY NO DIVERGENCE: my M2 interface contract + M3 layered context package included errors.py + main.py handlers as architectural/constraint context, so the corrected Task 2 prompt embedded 'raise HTTPException so main.py wraps in error_envelope; never return raw error dicts'. The context package WAS complete. ONE REAL QUIRK FOUND: the 401 message renders as 'missing [REDACTED]' on BOTH /links and /teams -- errors.py:15 redact() pattern 'Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-._~+/]+=*' matches the words 'bearer token' in the literal 'missing bearer token' and replaces it, so clients see a mangled message. This is PRE-EXISTING (present on /links before any team code existed), NOT agent-introduced, and identical on both endpoints -- so it is a codebase-level error-handling bug, not a convention divergence in my three outputs. Counterfactual that the drill is designed to catch: if my context package had OMITTED errors.py + main.py (the files defining the error format), a reasonable agent would have invented its own envelope (the module's example: {status:'error',message,statusCode} vs the real {error:{code,message,request_id}}) -- exactly the 'works in isolation, breaks every client parser' bug. The one missing-file check: which context file would have prevented a hypothetical mismatch? errors.py (the envelope definition) -- it was included, and that inclusion is what the empirical match proves. Verdict: no convention violation in the outputs; one pre-existing redaction quirk documented for the FIX step.
evidence: compare_errors.py + compare_errors2.py + compare_401.py: 15 live probes, all envelopes identical in shape
400/401/403/404/409 all wrapped by main.py handlers -> error_envelope; team and links identical
401 'missing [REDACTED]' on BOTH /links and /teams: pre-existing errors.py:15 redact() over-match, not agent divergence
No divergence in the three outputs; context package (errors.py + main.py included) was complete
